decision: Needs Fixes: raw adapter overhead reduced; end-to-end performance preservation and supported-hardware validation are not established
notes: Complete imported main85, preceding opt9 and current dense3 production Python; --lookup default; no prototype or runtime monkeypatch in timings.
Raw: GPU 1 / CPU affinity 4-7; two-rank pipelines: GPUs 1,2 / affinity 4-11. Shared PCIe Blackwell host, no NVLink or physical multi-node test.
128 features, batch 32, hotness 4, D=64, FP32/SGD; resident repeated keys, 20 warmups, six trials of 100 steps, five separately profiled steps.
Each six-process workload uses main,old,dense,dense,old,main order; the additional SparseDist reverse control uses dense,old,old,dense. Preserve all samples and outliers.
No other local GPU validation ran during these timed processes; external jobs and host scheduling still vary. End-to-end timings do not establish parity or a stable improvement.
Target stack: torch2.13/cu130, TorchRec1.8.0+0ea0ec0, FBGEMM1.8/cu130, NCCL2.30.7 headers/extension/preload with Torch2.29.7 dependency; not a certified single-NCCL NGC container.
Older stack: torch2.7/cu128, TorchRec/FBGEMM1.2, NCCL2.28.9 preload, no hierarchical ops; two-rank tests disable P2P/IB and use loopback.

No C++ or optimizer-format changes in this follow-up. Training extension/fatbin builds are the matching main85 plus publication refinement documented in input_dist_optimization_results.json; inference bindings disabled.
Dense3 production Python digest is 6cf177ccde3e6416c7eb7ab284a2bc606c9db6931bd86f20d5b65822f3f7d44b. Later test-only changes warm the initialization operator and add six half-cancellation cases.

Negative controls are separate staged runtime copies, not production changes. Removing record_stream fails; removing ready wait first passed due to lazy loading, then fails after exact-op warmup; normal warmed test passes.
Initial dense1 failure was a test fixture torch.full size argument, corrected before dense2; it is not a production-path defect.
